note: View-keeping descent of the fast race-cue pilot (haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.DescentViewConfig; visual_brain --descent-view on|off|DECLARATION, off by default, recorded in the flight-log sidecar under pilot_assistance.descent_view and descent_view_declaration, CSV columns view_sink_bound, view_withheld, view_boost only when on). Generic and course-agnostic: it reads the measured attitude and velocity, the visible ring cue state the pilot already has and the calibrated camera (30 deg up, focal 100 px at 320x180: lower image edge 12 deg below the body x axis); no height above ground, no course geometry, no per-course value. It answers the user's request of 2026-09-26 (Straw Bale downhill: 'increase throttle and pitch forward' instead of dropping onto the hill; touch the ground less). Diagnosis of straw-brain08-04/-06 (10 support-climb contacts, two spots per lap at y 161-166 and y 144-147) and -01 (the hillside slide): in the 3 s before every contact the pilot was 56-80% in 'below' at a requested 3.0-4.0 m/s (below_speed_fraction 0.5 of 6 m/s), each bottom clip began with a brake that pitched the nose 10-20 deg up (lower image edge up to +11 deg), requested descents were 16-30 deg (edge depression + a margin growing 5 -> 20 deg) against a lower image edge at -13 to -16 deg, so the measured flight path pointed below the image 70-79% of that time, into a hillside of about 12 deg; during contact the descent-path governor cut the horizontal request to 0.35-0.53x (straw-brain08-01 slid for 5 s at 0.35x with the throttle 0.37 below hover). The live logs also show the Straw rings 5-10 deg below the drone when seen with a level nose (inside a level camera's view) and a steady cruise pitch of only about -2 deg at 5-6 m/s (drag-light drone: speed alone does not lower the camera). The fast PD laps (straw-fast6-03) porpoise on the same downhill: brake (nose +12..+33) in 'below', then accelerate (nose -28..-45) in 'cue'. The values were chosen on development seeds of the offline surrogate with scoring-only hills (haltere.liftoff.descent_rehearsal: hill:6100-6111 and steep:5000-5007, fast PD and fast-brain-08; variants with a strict bound, with late steepening and with other margins, attitude filters and speed fractions were compared there, see the design notes), before the frozen gates (configs/pilot/descent_view_gates.json) and before any run of the gate seeds. The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze, and every version is reported. Surrogate results and open-loop replays are development evidence, never flight evidence.

descent_view_notes.view_bound: the pilot's own requested sink is bounded so that the flight path made of the measured horizontal velocity and the requested vertical speed points margin_deg (3 deg; cue_margin_deg 3 deg while the ring is in view) inside the camera's lower image edge at the measured attitude: exact projection through the calibrated camera, roll included (y/z <= tan(atan(cy/f) - margin) is linear in the vertical speed). With a level nose that is a path of 9 deg down at any speed; a nose-up (braking) drone may sink less, a hovering drone at most free_sink (0.3 m/s, a gentle touch at worst). The lowest in-view vertical speed per 1 m/s of horizontal speed is low-passed with attitude_time_constant (1 s): with the unfiltered attitude (and with 0.3 s) fast-brain-08's pitch and the bound formed a 0.6-1 Hz limit cycle in the development runs. A requested climb is never changed
descent_view_notes.keep_speed: below_speed_fraction 1: a bottom-clipped ring keeps the speed schedule (the default pilot halves it; that brake lifted the nose and the lower image edge on the Straw downhill). The descent-path governor is not fed while the bound withholds sink (a withheld sink is no shortfall) and never cuts below descent_min_scale (0.75; the default floor 0.35 held straw-brain08-01 on the hillside)
descent_view_notes.more_speed: while the bound withholds sink toward a ring ahead (states cue, below, below_weak) the horizontal request rises toward the speed schedule's, fully once boost_sink (0.3 m/s) is withheld; never above the declared speed (the brain contracts refuse more)
descent_view_notes.throttle_up: the requested sink grows at up to sink_acceleration (2.5 m/s^2 instead of the pilot's 5 m/s^2 slew), so a descent does not start with a deep throttle cut (the brain issued 0.3-0.35 below hover on the Straw descents)
descent_view_notes.steep_late: a ring that stays clipped below for more than late_after_s (0.75 s of the pilot's unbroken bottom clip) lies more steeply below than a steady view allows; the margin then falls at late_rate_deg_s (6 deg/s) down to late_max_deg (20 deg) below the lower image edge: a steep leg is flown shallow first (in view over a convex crest after the upper checkpoint) and steep late. Without it (a strict bound) the development runs overflew steep lower rings by up to 8 m and circled back (fast PD 2 -> 17-19 passes more than 1.5 m above a checkpoint, fast-brain-08 1 -> 18); with it the fast PD reached them more often (6) and faster. It is the part of the rule that points the path below the image, and only on legs steeper than the view
descent_view_notes.interactions: order in FastRaceCue.update: the pilot's request (search, launch and launch-surface rules first), then the view bound, then the descent-path governor, the speed rise and the support rule, then the looming governor and the vertical guard (which see the bounded request as the pilot's own), turn-first and the command slews. Search (no sink), launch and support climbs are unchanged; the slope-support rule needs a request below -0.8 m/s, which the bound allows only above about 5 m/s: a slow drone resting on a slope is not recognised by it. The rise toward the speed schedule is still capped by the looming governor's wall cap and by turn-first, which act later
descent_view_notes.brain_limit_found: fast-brain-08 does not keep 6 m/s while it sinks: asked for (6 m/s, -1.8 m/s) it flew about (3.0, -1.05) in the development runs, where asked for (3, -1.8) by the default pilot it tracked the request; its distillation data paired descents with the default pilot's half speed. With this rule it therefore descends shallower than asked and passes lower checkpoints high (1 -> 15 on the development hills) although its contacts fell 13 -> 3. A brain distilled under this pilot is the expected fix, not a pilot value

development_results.scope: surrogate with scoring-only hills on the development seeds only (hill:6100-6111, steep:5000-5007), 110 s, sim seed 17; per set: contacts, share of the descent time with the path below the image, passes > 1.5 m above a checkpoint, mean finish time; baseline -> this version (all courses finished, no crash in any run)

development_results.fast_pd_steep: contacts 5 -> 3, below view 30% -> 25%, high passes 1 -> 6, 62.6 s -> 55.3 s

development_results.brain08_steep: contacts 3 -> 1, below view 35% -> 36%, high passes 1 -> 6, 63.2 s -> 63.5 s

development_results.variants_compared: a strict bound without late steepening (attitude low-pass 0, 0.3 and 1 s): fast PD hill high passes 17-19 and fast-brain-08 12-18, with circling back to overflown rings (brain-08 +11-12% time); late steepening after 0.5-1 s at 4-8 deg/s; a 0 deg in-view margin with a 0.5 descent floor; a 0.75 below-speed fraction: none brought fast-brain-08's high passes below 15; this version was the fast PD's best compromise and within brain-08's range. The design seeds differ from every gate seed.
